title: Transfers of personal data out of the Union (GDPR, Chapter V)
about: May personal data be transferred to a third country, on what ground and with what safeguards. The rules are Chapter V of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 with Articles 3 and 4, the standard contractual clauses of Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 and the EU-US adequacy decision (EU) 2023/1795, each clause in the words of the Official Journal; the readings are the Court of Justice's, each passage found in its judgment. Standing on 15 November 2026: Decision 2023/1795 was upheld by the General Court (Latombe, T-553/23) and an appeal is pending (C-703/25 P); Bindl (T-354/22) is under appeal (C-206/25 P); the protocol amending Convention 108 (CETS 223) is not in force. Not encoded yet: binding corporate rules in detail, codes and certifications, Article 48, the second subparagraph of Article 49(1), onward transfers, and the lawfulness of the processing itself (Articles 5, 6, 9, 28). The treaty frame is given as texts; no rule of this scheme states it. A scheme is its author's reading of the law, to be checked against the clauses it cites; it is not legal advice.

provisions.label: Article 17(1)
provisions.text: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary or unlawful interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to unlawful attacks on his honour and reputation.

provisions.label: Article 17(2)
provisions.text: Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks.

instruments.title: Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (1950), as amended
instruments.kind: a treaty of the Council of Europe; the frame, stated by no rule of this scheme

provisions.label: Article 8(1)
provisions.text: Everyone has the right to respect for his private and family life, his home and his correspondence.

provisions.label: Article 8(2)
provisions.text: There shall be no interference by a public authority with the exercise of this right except such as is in accordance with the law and is necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security, public safety or the economic well-being of the country, for the prevention of disorder or crime, for the protection of health or morals, or for the protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

instruments.title: Convention 108 (ETS No. 108, 1981) and its Additional Protocol (ETS No. 181, 2001), the texts in force
instruments.kind: treaties of the Council of Europe; the frame, stated by no rule of this scheme. The amending protocol CETS No. 223 is not in force

provisions.label: ETS 108, Article 12(2)
provisions.text: A Party shall not, for the sole purpose of the protection of privacy, prohibit or subject to special authorisation transborder flows of personal data going to the territory of another Party.

provisions.label: ETS 181, Article 2(1)
provisions.text: Each Party shall provide for the transfer of personal data to a recipient that is subject to the jurisdiction of a State or organisation that is not Party to the Convention only if that State or organisation ensures an adequate level of protection for the intended data transfer.

holdings.name: Breyer
holdings.passage: constitutes personal data within the meaning of that provision, in relation to that provider, where the latter has the legal means which enable it to identify the data subject
holdings.note: On Article 2(a) of Directive 95/46, whose definition Article 4(1) of the Regulation carries over.

holdings.passage: pseudonymised data must not be regarded as constituting, in all cases and for every person, personal data
